I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt (386/387 files SHA-256 verified; LICENSE elided, export.sh self-referential) and found the cause of the failure. I then verified it against a real PostgreSQL, so this is observed rather than reasoned.

The failure
TheSchemaRefusesEveryForbiddenShapeOfAnEventRow probes the vocabulary constraint with ('loved', 'Anything'). That row breaks two CHECKs at once — ..._type_vocabulary ('loved' is not in the list) and ..._body_payload ((event_type='submitted') = (body IS NOT NULL) is false = true). PostgreSQL evaluates CHECKs in name order, so body_payload sorts first and is the name reported. The assertion reached past what it could decide.

Confirmed empirically just now:

loved + 'Anything'  -> body_payload        (the failure you saw)
loved + NULL        -> type_vocabulary     (the repair)
The repair (F-123)
Each probe row now breaks exactly one constraint, and that property is itself proven rather than assumed: every probe is paired with a control row differing in one attribute, inserted inside a transaction and rolled back. If a probe were over-determined, its control would be refused too and the fact fails by name. Verified against the real DDL — all five probes name their own constraint, all four controls insert, final row count 0.

The fifth probe (body_within_cap) is added, plus a catalogue assertion that the table's CHECK set is exactly those four — so "every forbidden shape" is now computed rather than claimed. Still 13 [Fact]; §16.4's count does not move.

The container chatter (F-124)
Testcontainers logs every create, readiness probe and delete at Information through its own console logger — several hundred lines that buried the one failing assertion. Both fixtures now set TestcontainersSettings.Logger = NullLogger.Instance as the first statement inside their existing try, where a throw still becomes a skip. What diagnoses a container that won't start here is the fixture's own DescribeFailure prose, which is better than those lines anyway.

Gated by a new ContainerLoggingContractTests — 2 assertions, subjects computed from the tree (files constructing a PostgreSqlBuilder, floor of 2), asserting each installs the logger and installs it before it builds. Both proven sensitive against planted defects.

I have the code changes done and verified but ran out of tool budget before writing the documentation updates and packaging the tarball. Nothing is delivered yet — say the word and I'll finish the slice: the five source files plus TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (§16.4 paragraphs, Appendix A rows F-123/F-124, v1.54 changelog), DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md (two ledger rows), BUILD_PROGRESS.md (Slice 69 row, narrative, test arithmetic 1320 → 1322), and MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, packaged as one extractable .tar.gz. No files need deleting.

Claude reached its tool-use limit for this turn.

Extract at the repository root: tar -xzf myrestaurant-slice-69.tar.gz. Nine full files, repo-relative paths, no scripts.

Nothing to delete. One file needs git add:

tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Deployment/ContainerLoggingContractTests.cs
No production code changed. 0009_menu_item_comments.sql and Menu/MenuItemComments.cs are untouched — the schema was correct the whole time.

What the three findings are
F-123 — the failure. The probe offered ('loved', 'Anything') to the vocabulary CHECK, but that row also breaks body_payload (false = true). PostgreSQL sorts a relation's CHECKs by name and reports the first refusal, so body_payload won. Each probe now breaks exactly one CHECK, and a control row differing in one attribute — inserted in a transaction, rolled back — proves it. The four constraint names come out of pg_constraint rather than a list, and the cap gets the fifth probe the fact's name had been promising. Executed against a real PostgreSQL: five probes, five distinct names, four controls accepted, zero rows left, and the old row reproduces your exact failure.

F-124 — why it shipped. Slice 68's narrative described four mutation runs of 0009; six paragraphs below, the same slice says no container engine ran. A planted-defect proof presupposes a green baseline, and this one was red. That paragraph is corrected in place, and §18 now separates proven by execution from reasoned, not run.

F-125 — the chatter. Several hundred Testcontainers Information lines per run were what buried the one failing assertion. Both fixtures now assign TestcontainersSettings.Logger = NullLogger.Instance as the first statement of the try that already turns a container failure into a skip — so it can't crash an assembly — and after ContainerEngineDiscovery has set DOCKER_HOST, since touching TestcontainersSettings snapshots the endpoint. That ordering is the second of the two new assertions.

Expected test count
1322 = 1320 + 2. MenuItemCommentTests still holds thirteen [Fact]; the new probe and the catalogue comparison live inside the existing fact. §16.4 census 46 → 47 over a floor of 37. Spec v1.54, findings floor F-125.

All gates emulated green: census, version header, Markdown tables, byte hygiene, no-comment, archived-link, image references. Three veto points are in _CHANGES.md with reversion instructions — the most likely to interest you is that NullLogger drops Warning and Error too, and the note says exactly how to swap in a Warning threshold without touching the gate.
